question.text: Why is time stamping mandatory for all mutual fund transactions?

answer.text: To calculate the expense ratio applicable to the transaction
To verify the identity of the investor
To determine the applicable NAV based on the cut-off timing
To comply with income tax reporting requirements

explanation.text: The Logic: Time stamping records the exact time a transaction request is received at an Official Point of Acceptance (OPoA). The applicable NAV is determined by the time stamp at the OPoA against the relevant cut-off. For online transactions the web-server time of the OPoA is used. The Trap: The time at which the investor submits an application to a distributor is not the NAV-determining time. Distributors must forward applications to an OPoA, and only the OPoA's time stamp governs which NAV applies. Note: Source: NISM Series V-A (Mutual Fund Distributors) workbook, pp.192-193 — applicable NAV is determined by time stamping at OPoAs; distributor receipt time and web-server time for online transactions.
